messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired -> Summary: p95 latency SLO burn on inference-gateway (us-west). p95=620ms (SLO 450ms). PD: PD#INC-33211. Paging on-call.

sarah (oncall): Acked via PD. I'm on it, pulling graphs.

emily (sre): grabbing grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/inference/p95; seeing a sharp jump at 17:12 UTC that correlates with increased KV cache miss rate.

kevin (prod-eng): Any recent deploys?

sarah (oncall): Not in prod at 17:10 per deploy-bot. No canary rollouts.

ops-bot: Deploy bot: no deploy events in the last 60m.

josh (support): Are customers affected? any high-severity accounts?

emily (sre): Short answer: small fraction of requests on /v1/generate and /v1/embed with context lengths >1024. Tail latency jumps when KV cache miss + longer decode.

kevin (prod-eng): That points at KV cache eviction surge. Could be a jittered workload or new traffic shape. Can we check k-v eviction metrics and sidecar logs?

emily (sre): Looking. sidecar.kv.evictions spike at 17:11 -> 17:13. Also see throttling in the sidecar logs: `WARN kv: eviction_pressure=true`.

sarah (oncall): Trying mitigation path from runbook: 1) reduce burst by temp rate limit 2) increase hotpath capacity 3) warm cache.

kevin (prod-eng): I'll trigger a short autoscaler emergency scale for inference-gateway-us-west (add 3 nodes), ETA ~2m.

ops-bot: Autoscaler request submitted: scale +3 nodes (reason: emergency p95). ETA 120s.

josh (support): Drafting internal customer note in #support-alerts: "Seeing elevated p95 for a subset of inference requests in us-west; mitigation in progress. We'll follow up in 15m."

sarah (oncall): Also enabling temporary route-level throttling on `embed` route at 5rps/client-id to reduce KV churn. Applying now.

kevin (prod-eng): Command applied:
```
PATCH /config/routes/embed
{ "rate_limit": "5rps" }
```

emily (sre): Cache warm job started: rehydrate hot prefixes from recent logs to local KV. Script: `scripts/rehydrate_kv.sh --prefixes recent-hot -c us-west`

incident-bot: PD update: alert status -> acknowledged by sarah (oncall).

~90s later~

emily (sre): Autoscaler finished. +3 nodes are healthy. KV eviction rate dropping. p95 back to ~480ms (still above 450).

sarah (oncall): Good. Keep monitoring. Is there any single slow model version?

emily (sre): A few requests hitting model `redwood-base-10b-quant` at long seq length look worse. But the main factor was eviction + cold KV lookups.

kevin (prod-eng): We should consider a short canary rollback for the latest quantization kernel for that model if we see more degradation. Not yet.

josh (support): Customer note updated with ETA 15m and mention to contact support if they see errors.

sarah (oncall): I'm handing this to devon (day shift) for watch-and-verify. Handoff notes: autoscaled +3, embed route throttled, cache rehydrate in progress, p95 ~480. Please escalate if p95 >550 again.

@devon (oncall-next): Got it, taking over. I'll keep PD open and monitor for 30m.

incident-bot: PD note -> Status changed to "investigating" -> "monitoring".

devon (oncall-next): Quick list for follow-up: 1) confirm no upstream client changed request patterns 2) look for unusual traffic fanout 3) check dedicated customer routes for SLA impact.

josh (support): FYI, support rota flagged one mid-enterprise org with slight latency increase but no errors; proactively pinged their SRE.

emily (sre): Closing loop: KV rehydrate finished, eviction rate normalized, sidecar logs show no further warnings. p95 stabilized at ~430ms now.

sarah (oncall): Thanks. I'm clearing PD page: moving to resolved if no regressions in 30m. :white_check_mark:

devon (oncall-next): I'll leave monitoring for the next 30m and then close. Handed off cleanly.

josh (support): Posting post-incident note draft in #incidents after 30m with customer impact summary and mitigation steps.

incident-bot: PD update -> incident resolved by devon (oncall-next).

sarah (oncall): Postmortem owners: emily + kevin. Please include root cause (KV eviction surge) and follow-ups: tighter hot-prefix warming, route prewarming for long-context requests, and alert tuning to reduce noisy autopager floods.

kevin (prod-eng): Adding follow-ups: 1) autoscaler headroom policy adjust 2) increase KV cache retention for hot prefixes 3) add a synthetic test for long-context p95 in us-west.

emily (sre): Will add timeline and metrics. Draft ready in #postmortems in ~1h.

devon (oncall-next): Closing thread — monitoring window ended, no regressions.

-- end of thread --
